title: The dispatch label leads with the seat role when one is given
action: In prepare.rs, the non-cell subject (`let subject = if kind == "cell" {` … `else { match purpose … Some(p) => format!("{kind}: {}", …), None => kind.to_string() }`, rg hit prepare.rs:1587-1601) leads with the ASKED role when `--role` was given (the canonical `role: Option<&str>` local at prepare.rs:1323, config spelling), and with the kind otherwise: `hat-facts-gaps: hat wave … (opus)`, `extraction: … (haiku)`; no `--role` keeps today's bytes (`gather: … (sonnet)`, `gather (sonnet)`). Cell subjects unchanged. Extend the doc comment above ("Every other kind: subject is …") with the reason: an advisor-kind dispatch carrying a seat role read as 'advisor' in every UI even when the seat's own model ran — the label must name the slot that resolved. Red first: add a test in drivers/tests.rs that `--kind advisor --role hat-facts-gaps --purpose "hat wave"` on a host with `hat-facts-gaps: opus, advisor: fable` yields description `hat-facts-gaps: hat wave (opus)`; watch it fail with `advisor: hat wave (opus)`; then fix. Keep the existing no-role description tests green untouched.

truths: --kind advisor --role hat-facts-gaps --purpose X → description 'hat-facts-gaps: X (<seat model>)'
no --role → description bytes identical to today

artifacts.substantive: role-led subject with its comment and a red-first test

key_links: the description reads the same canonical role local the resolver reads
prohibitions: No change to marker, model, or subagent_type
